newsitem.title: USA: BellSouth Q2 EPS rise 12.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: BellSouth Q2 EPS rise 12.7 pct.

text.p: BellSouth Corp on Monday reported second quarter operating earnings up 12.7 percent from a year earlier and slightly above Wall Street estimates.
The company said its strong results were led by the installation of record numbers of additional lines and high growth in convenience features and wireless operations.

Sales of BellSouth's calling features and convenience services continued to grow at a rate of 25 percent or more, it said. Total features activated rose 25 percent to 33.4 million, while revenues for such features as call waiting and MemoryCall voice messaging rose 26 percent to $322 million.
The company's domestic wireless division posted customer growth of 21 percent from a year ago in the second quarter. International wireless operations saw growth of 83 percent.
Domestic cellular revenues rose 11.5 percent to $625.7 million. International cellular revenues grew 65.9 percent to $382.9 million.
Minutes of use along the company's interstate access line network grew to 18.6 million from 16.8 million, and along its intrastate network grew to 5.9 million from 5.2 million.
"Excellent earnings out of BellSouth," Montgomery Securities analyst Bill Vogel said. "We are pretty bullish on the rest of the year. Everything we saw in the quarter looks great."
Vogel said he is maintaining a 12- to 18-month price target of $52 on the stock. BellSouth shares were up 1-1/16 at 46-1/8 shortly before midday on the New York Stock Exchange.
